questions.stem: An unknown element conducts electricity, has a high melting point, and forms a basic oxide. The element is most likely:
questions.explanation: These properties are characteristic of metals: electrical conductivity, high melting point, and forming basic oxides. Magnesium is a metal that fits all these criteria. Sulfur and chlorine are non-metals, and while carbon can conduct electricity (as graphite), it forms acidic oxides (CO₂), not basic ones.

options.text: Gain electrons to form negative ions
Share electrons to form covalent bonds
Lose electrons to form positive ions

questions.explanation: Metals have relatively few electrons in their outer shell (1, 2, or 3 typically). When they react, they lose these outer electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration, forming positive ions (cations). For example, sodium loses 1 electron to form Na⁺. Non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions.

questions.stem: A student tests two oxides. Oxide A dissolves in water to form a solution with pH 3. Oxide B dissolves in water to form a solution with pH 12. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A is a metal oxide and B is a non-metal oxide
A is a non-metal oxide and B is a metal oxide

questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions (pH below 7), so Oxide A (pH 3) is likely a non-metal oxide. Metal oxides dissolve in water to form alkaline solutions (pH above 7), so Oxide B (pH 12) is likely a metal oxide. For example, SO₂ forms sulfurous acid (acidic), while Na₂O forms NaOH (alkaline).

questions.stem: Where are metals found in the Periodic Table?

options.text: On the right side of the Periodic Table
On the left side and centre of the Periodic Table
Only in the transition metals block

questions.explanation: Metals are found on the left side and centre of the Periodic Table, making up the majority of elements. Non-metals are found on the right side. The dividing line (staircase) runs roughly from boron to astatine. Group 1, Group 2, and the transition metals are all metallic.

questions.stem: Which property makes metals suitable for use as electrical wiring?

options.text: They have delocalised electrons that can carry charge

questions.explanation: Metals conduct electricity because they contain delocalised (free) electrons that can move through the metal structure to carry electrical charge. Copper is commonly used for wiring because it is an excellent conductor and is also ductile (can be drawn into wires). High density and high melting points are not relevant to electrical conduction.
